input.question: How can I go to sleep extremely hungry/thirsty yet wake up and not feel the hunger/thirst at all?
input.ground_truth: After the energy of the food you consumed is used up, your blood sugar drops and the body enters a fasting state. The liver releases small doses of glucose by breaking down glycogen to maintain your blood sugar (in your case while sleeping). So when you wake up your blood sugar is at the right level and you don't feel hungry.

Okay! Imagine you are a teddy bear at bedtime.

At night, you feel really, really hungry or thirsty. Maybe your tummy is rumbling or your mouth feels dry. But then you close your eyes and fall asleep.

When you are sleeping, your body is resting and your brain is taking a little nap too. While you are dreaming about cookies or drinking juice, your body doesn’t notice the hunger or thirst as much. It’s kind of like how you might not hear a little noise when you are deep in a fun dream.

When you wake up in the morning, your body feels better because you have been resting, and sometimes you forget about the hunger or thirst for a little while. It’s like when you are playing and you don’t notice you are thirsty until later!

But soon, your tummy or mouth might remind you again, “Hey! I’m still hungry or thirsty!” That’s your body’s way of telling you it needs food or water.

So, being asleep makes you not notice those feelings for a while, but your body still needs them when you wake up!
